input.body:
label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits the input on "\n" only (`lines = text.split("\n")`) and does not strip a leading UTF-8 BOM or trailing "\r" from Windows-style CRLF line endings. The new Windows accounting export tool likely emits a BOM and/or CRLF line endings, which corrupts the header/first field and causes the column count check in `splitFields`/row validation to fail, always on row 1. The parser needs to normalize line endings (CRLF -> LF) and strip a BOM before splitting/parsing rows.

text: This matches the CSV parser logic — the new Windows export tool likely introduces CRLF line endings or a BOM, which `parser.ts`'s naive `split("\n")` doesn't handle, causing column count mismatches on row 1.
